meta.about: In 1995, the group was restructured and thus was formed Cadila Healthcare under the aegis of the Zydus group. From a humble turnover Rs. 250 crores in 1995 the group witnessed a significant financial growth and registered a turnover of over Rs. 14,253 crores in FY20. Adhering to its brand promise of being dedicated to life in all its dimensions, Zydus continues to innovate with an unswerving focus to address the unmet healthcare needs. Simultaneously it rededicates itself to its mission of creating healthier, happier communities across the globe
meta.keyPoints: Business Segments: a) North America Formulations (40% of Q4 FY26 revenue): Co. ranked 3rd among US generic companies by generic TRx, a gain of 2 positions over the last 4 years. During Q4 FY26, 6 new products were launched, 3 ANDAs filed, and 9 ANDAs approved. For full year FY26, 30 ANDAs were filed and 26 approved including 6 tentative approvals. Cumulative filings stand at 508 and cumulative approvals at 435 including 26 tentative.[1] b) India Formulations Business (24% of Q4 FY26 revenue):[2] The company has 10 brands with value above Rs 1,000 mn, 24 between Rs 500-1,000 mn, and 35 between INR 250-500 mn. Key product launches in Q4 FY26 include Tishtha - world's first biosimilar of Nivolumab, Anyra - India's first indigenously developed biosimilar of Aflibercept 2 mg, and Semaglutide injection under three brands - Semaglyn, Mashema, and Alterme. c) Consumer Wellness (20% of Q4 FY26 revenue):[3] The company operates in 2 different segments viz. personal care segment comprising the Nycil and Everyuth brands and food and nutrition segment through the brands Glucon-D, Sugar Free, Complan, and Nutralite.[4] Glucon-D holds ~59% market share (Rank 1), Nycil holds ~33% (Rank 1), Sugar Free holds ~96% (Rank 1). In the Everyuth range, Scrub holds ~49% share (Rank 1) and Peel Off holds ~75% (Rank 1), while Facial Cleansing holds ~8% (Rank 5). Complan holds 4% fat spread share (Rank 4). Nutralite is Rank 1 in fat spread by company estimates. RiteBite and Max Protein are Rank 1 in Nutrition & Protein Bar and Protein Cookies & Chips by company estimates. d) International Markets Formulations (11% of Q4 FY26 revenue): The company's international markets division comprises of the Emerging Markets (selected territories in Asia Pacific, Middle East, Africa and Latin America) and Europe (France, Spain and the UK). In emerging markets, co. adopted a focused, therapy led approach, tailoring the offerings to meet the needs of specific markets. In Europe, focus remains on broadening the portfolio and enhance the market coverage.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Zydus Lifesciences (consolidated, Rs crore). Zydus reports three segments (Pharmaceuticals, Consumer Products = Zydus Wellness, Medical Technologies = mainly Amplitude Surgical) and discloses revenue by business; it does not disclose EBITDA by business, so the engine runs on one revenue-growth path and a consolidated EBITDA margin (company basis: EBITDA includes the forex gains Zydus books inside other expenses, Rs1,280 cr in FY26 and Rs57 cr in Q1FY27). The business-line build (US$ North America x Rs/$, India formulations, international markets, APIs, alliances, Consumer Wellness, MedTech, other operating revenue) is in `businessLines` and is checked against model revenue in tools/authoring/ZYDUSLIFE.ctx.js. Profit is attributable to owners (ZYDUSLIFE.patch.js puts Screener's Net Profit on the 'Profit for EPS' basis); the tax line carries tax plus the 42.41% minority in Zydus Wellness, net of the tax-free JV share (built in `taxBuild`). Engine workarounds: (1) the Mirabegron licence fee (US$75 mn prepaid on 10-Feb-2026, amortised over 19 months to Sep-2027) is reported inside D&A; the engine has one depreciation rate, so the licence amortisation is carried as a negative item inside other income (`otherIncomeBuild`), and reported-basis D&A = engine depreciation + licence amortisation; (2) the Rs1,100 cr buyback of Jun-2026 (8,730,158 shares at Rs1,260) is carried as part of the FY27E payout (the engine has no buyback line), and the per-share target uses the post-buyback count of 99.75 cr shares through an implied multiple written by tools/authoring/ZYDUSLIFE.mult.js; (3) the Assertio acquisition (US$166.4 mn, completed 16-Jun-2026) is carried in FY27E capex because the engine has no acquisitions line; its purchase price is mostly intangibles that are amortised like capex. Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the business-line build (`businessLines`): FY26 revenue from operations Rs27,148 cr = North America Rs11,682 cr (US$1,323 mn) + India formulations Rs6,574 cr + international markets Rs3,070 cr + APIs Rs641 cr + alliances Rs59 cr + Consumer Wellness Rs3,913 cr + MedTech Rs780 cr + other operating revenue Rs429 cr (Q4FY26 presentation; FY26 business-wise sales Rs267,197 mn). FY27E +17.8% to Rs31,987 cr (Q1FY27 +22%; management guided 'high teens' in May-2026 and 'strong double-digit' in Aug-2026; PL Rs32,207 cr, MOSL Rs32,242 cr). About 6 points of FY27E growth are acquisitions annualising (Comfort Click from 29-Aug-2025, Amplitude from 29-Jul-2025, Assertio from Q2FY27) and ~4 points the weaker rupee (FY26 average Rs88.3/US$, Rs95.81 on 30-Sep-2026). FY28E +8.7% (gMirabegron erosion, Saroglitazar launch year, no acquisitions annualising) and FY29E +10.3% (Saroglitazar and biosimilars ramping).
assumptions._marginWhy: Company-basis EBITDA margin (= Screener operating profit; includes forex gains booked in other expenses). History: 27.5% FY24, 30.4% FY25, 31.2% FY26 (26.8% excluding Rs1,198 cr of operating forex gains), 24.1% in Q1FY27 (23.4% excluding the Rs57 cr forex gain). The step down is gRevlimid's end (volume-limited exclusivity; Zydus's sales were 'very little' in Q3FY26 and nil from Q4FY26), lower-margin acquired businesses (Comfort Click, Amplitude), the Mirabegron per-unit licence fee (in cost of goods until Sep-2027) and Saroglitazar pre-launch spending (~US$70 mn in FY27, mostly H2). FY27E 24.0%: management guides '~24%' including Saroglitazar (11-Aug-2026); other expenses ex-R&D at Rs1,900-2,000 cr a quarter; R&D ~8% of revenue. FY28E 23.5%: the Saroglitazar launch year (US launch targeted Apr-2027; 'the first 2 years will be a build-out phase') and more generic competition in Mirabegron, partly offset by India/EM mix and a full year of Rolvedon. FY29E 24.5%: Saroglitazar and specialty revenue scaling (management aims for 28-30% 'as we move closer to the 5-year period'). Street: FY27E 23.8% (PL, ex-forex), 24.2% (MOSL); FY28E 24.1% (PL), 23.4% (MOSL), 22.8% (JM).
assumptions._capexWhy: Organic capex Rs1,214 cr (FY25) and Rs1,714.5 cr (FY26; Q4FY26 presentation); Q1FY27 Rs585 cr. FY27E guidance Rs1,500-1,600 cr (11-Aug-2026 call: SEZ-3, capacity at Moraiya, Goa, Baddi and SEZ units, a new formulations R&D centre, a one-off land purchase for Zydus Wellness, a CAR-T facility, a vaccine drug-substance plant, Zylidac). FY27E = Rs1,550 cr organic + Rs1,594 cr for Assertio (US$166.4 mn at ~Rs95.8/US$; engine workaround: no acquisitions line; Assertio's purchase price is mostly brand and platform intangibles, per the CFO). FY28-29E Rs1,500 cr a year (~4% of revenue).
assumptions._depWhy: Engine depreciation excludes the Mirabegron licence amortisation (carried in `otherIncomeBuild`). FY26 reported D&A Rs1,408 cr = 5.0% of average gross block (Rs28,005 cr incl. acquired intangibles). Q1FY27 reported D&A Rs554.7 cr includes ~Rs104.6 cr of licence amortisation (US$75 mn = Rs662.5 cr over 19 months, AR FY26 note 30), so the base run-rate is ~Rs450 cr a quarter (Rs1,800 cr a year), plus Assertio purchase-price amortisation from Q2FY27 (not in Q1, CFO) and new capex. 5.45% of average gross block gives Rs1,956 / 2,082 / 2,164 cr; with the licence amortisation (Rs418 / 187 / 0 cr) reported D&A is Rs2,374 / 2,269 / 2,164 cr (PL Rs2,219 cr FY27E and Rs2,375 cr FY28E; MOSL Rs2,158 cr FY27E). CWIP (Rs3,698 cr on Screener, incl. Rs2,533 cr of intangibles under development) is held flat by the engine.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Zydus is a net borrower (net debt Rs4,305 cr at Mar-26 and Rs5,904 cr at Jun-26, company basis), so the engine's treasury line is negative and earns nothing; treasury interest is built explicitly in `otherIncomeBuild` from the gross cash and investments Zydus still holds (Rs7,464 cr at Mar-26: current investments Rs5,776 cr, cash Rs855 cr, bank balances Rs561 cr and other liquid holdings) and interest cost is entered separately. Screener's net cash (Rs-3,539 cr at Mar-26) differs from the company's net debt because it adds the JV stakes (Rs1,167 cr, equity method) and deducts lease liabilities (Rs727 cr).
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built in `otherIncomeBuild` from sourced parts: treasury and other income Rs400 / 380 / 360 cr + share of JV profit (Zydus Takeda, Bayer Zydus; tax-paid) Rs100 / 110 / 120 cr - Mirabegron licence amortisation Rs418 / 187 / 0 cr (engine workaround). Before the licence item: Rs500 / 490 / 480 cr against Rs607 cr in FY26 (other income Rs509.5 cr + JV Rs97.1 cr, AR FY26 notes 4 and 34) and Rs561 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26 as filed (other income Rs460.7 cr + JV Rs100.5 cr). The gap to FY26 is the smaller treasury after Rs7,000+ cr of acquisitions and the buyback: FY26 included a swap gain of Rs38 cr and fair-value gains of Rs29 cr, which we do not repeat. Exceptional items (Screener nets them into other income: Rs-516.6 cr in FY26, Rs-18.2 cr in Q1FY27) are not forecast.

assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs438.9 cr (interest Rs365 cr: term loans Rs156 cr, short-term loans Rs172 cr, leases Rs5 cr, others Rs31 cr; unwinding of contingent consideration on LiqMeds and other deals Rs63 cr; other Rs11 cr, AR FY26 note 39). Checked each year in ZYDUSLIFE.ctx.js.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY27E includes the Jun-2026 buyback (Rs1,100 cr: 8,730,158 shares at Rs1,260, offer 4-10 Jun-2026, shares extinguished by 29-Jun-2026) plus the FY26 final dividend of Re1 a share (~Rs100 cr): Rs1,200 cr = 31.8% of FY27E profit (engine workaround: there is no buyback line, so the FY27E dividend per share shown by the model, ~Rs12, is really Re1 of dividend plus the buyback). dcf._betaWhy: Pharma is defensive (below-market sensitivity); modest leverage (net debt ~0.7x EBITDA at Jun-26). Beta 0.85 gives a cost of equity of 11.6%; the engine discounts at the cost of equity, which is close to a WACC with ~5% debt in the capital structure.
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; Zydus is half US generics (low single-digit growth in dollars, ~2% rupee depreciation) and half branded India/EM/consumer (high single digit). House range 5-6%: 5.5%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% (FY29E) to 7% over 15 years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades from 24.5% to 25%: the branded mix rises (management aims for 28-30%), but US generic price erosion and new launches' costs recur; we do not assume the 31% of FY26, which included gRevlimid and Rs1,280 cr of forex gains.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex moves from ~4% of revenue (FY28-29E) to 4.5%: FY26 organic capex of Rs1,715 cr (6.3% of revenue) included new plants; maintenance plus growth capex for a branded-plus-generics portfolio is ~4.5%.

bull.narrative: Saroglitazar is approved on time and launches well in PBC (heading to the upper end of the US$200-300 mn peak range), US generics hold US$330 mn+ a quarter as Mirabegron competition stays limited, India keeps growing ~15% and international markets ~20%; EBITDA margin climbs back above 25% by FY28-29E.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Saroglitazar is delayed or launches slowly against two entrenched PPAR agonists, gMirabegron and other key US products erode faster (US sales back to ~US$280 mn a quarter), the acquired businesses (Comfort Click, Amplitude, Zylidac) disappoint and an FDA problem hits a key site; EBITDA margin ~22%, the FY22-FY23 level.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Zydus: P/E on 12-month-forward or FY28E consolidated EPS (PL 25x FY28E, MOSL 23x 12-month forward, JM 24x Mar-28, Sharekhan 20x FY28E). Our multiple: Zydus's own one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 on EPS before exceptional items and the FY22 animal-health sale gain (trough years excluded), times the pharma sector factor (+5.45%, PLAYBOOK §7c), nearest half-turn. Applied to EPS per post-buyback share (99.75 cr shares); the engine carries it as an implied multiple of its own Sep-28E EPS (on the FY26 count of 100.62 cr shares), written by tools/authoring/ZYDUSLIFE.mult.js.

cover.headline: The windfall years are over; the stock still prices them in
cover.lead: Zydus is India's #1 oncology company, the #3 generic supplier in the US by prescriptions and the owner of Sugar Free, Glucon-D and Complan. FY26 was its best year ever: ₹27,148 cr of revenue and a 31.2% EBITDA margin, lifted by two limited-competition US generics (gRevlimid and generic Myrbetriq) and ₹1,198 cr of forex gains. Q1FY27 showed the reset: revenue +22% (acquisitions, India +20%, international +34%) but EBITDA −8%, margin 24.1% and attributable profit −36%. The street values Zydus on **P/E on one-year-forward EPS (23-25x FY28E)**. We forecast EPS of ₹37.5 / ₹42.8 / ₹53.4 for FY27-29E, below the street. Zydus's own forward P/E since Apr-2021 has a median of 18.4x on EPS before one-offs; times the pharma sector factor (+5.45%) that gives **19.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹48.5 (per post-buyback share) = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**. **We initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks are higher (EV/EBITDA ₹1,215 before minorities, DCF ₹1,183), and we say why below. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The US engine is smaller without its windfalls
arguments.p: US sales were US$372 mn in Q1FY26 and US$313-327 mn a quarter since gRevlimid's volume limits ran out (end-Jan-2026). Generic Myrbetriq now carries a licence fee to Astellas until Sep-2027 and faces more competitors. Rolvedon (Assertio, US$15-20 mn a quarter), 505(b)(2) launches and biosimilars help, but management only guides "around single-digit growth". We model US$ sales +{{as.businessLines.naUsdGrowth.0|n1}}% / +{{as.businessLines.naUsdGrowth.1|n1}}% / +{{as.businessLines.naUsdGrowth.2|n1}}% for FY27-29E.

arguments.h: India, emerging markets and specialty are real, and growing
arguments.p: India formulations grew 20% in Q1FY27 against a market growing ~10-11%, with a rising chronic share (54%), first-in-world biosimilars (nivolumab) and in-house NCEs (saroglitazar, desidustat). International markets grew 40% in FY26. US branded sales are 10-11% of US sales and should pass 15% this year. This is the part of Zydus that deserves a premium; it is ~40% of revenue.

arguments.h: Acquisitions add revenue, not much EPS (yet)
arguments.p: Zydus spent ₹7,000+ cr on deals in 15 months (Amplitude, Comfort Click, Agenus plants, Assertio) and ₹1,100 cr on a buyback. They lift FY27E revenue by ~6 points but bring amortisation, interest and a 42% minority in Zydus Wellness. D&A plus interest rise from 15% of EBITDA in FY25 to ~39% in FY27E. We forecast EPS falling to {{F.eps.0|inr}} in FY27E and growing ~2% a year FY26-29E, versus EBITDA margins of {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.1|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}}.

arguments.h: Valuation: the market pays more than Zydus's own history
arguments.p: At ₹1,162 the stock trades at 26.9x our FY28E EPS and 24.0x Sep-28E, against an 18.4x median since 2021 (25th-75th percentile 13.0-24.0x). Part of the low history is the gRevlimid years, when the market refused to pay for windfall EPS; we cannot strip that out because Zydus never disclosed gRevlimid's sales. Even at the street's 23x, our target would be ~₹1,120: close to today's price, not well above it.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): the first quarter with Assertio (Rolvedon) and its amortisation, Saroglitazar pre-launch spending and US sales after Mirabegron competition.
Saroglitazar (PBC) NDA: priority review, approval expected by Q4FY27; US launch targeted Apr-2027 on Zydus's own front end (peak sales guided at US$200-300 mn).
Mirabegron: the licence fee ends in Sep-2027; how many generics enter and when (settlement terms confidential).
India: semaglutide (three brands plus Lupin and Torrent co-marketing), biosimilars (nivolumab, aflibercept), growth vs the IPM (+10.7% in Aug-2026).
US price-fixing litigation: Zydus is a defendant in five bellwether trials scheduled for 2026-2028; FDA inspections at acquired sites (LiqMeds UK, Zylidac California).

sections.title: Two different industries: a 10%-growth Indian brand market and a price-taking US generics market

blocks.p: **India.** The Indian pharmaceutical market (IPM) grew 8.3% in FY25 with volumes up only 1.3%: growth comes from price and new products, not more pills. It sped up in FY26 and 2026 (10.1% in Mar-2026, 10.7% in Aug-2026), and Pharmarack raised its 2026 forecast to 11.3%. Chronic therapies (cardiac, diabetes, oncology) grow faster than acute. Zydus's chronic sales grew 15.8% against 12% for the market (MAT Jun-2026). Price controls and trade generics cap the upside; differentiated launches (biosimilars, new molecules, semaglutide after patent expiry in Mar-2026) are where share is won.

**US generics.** The US is the world's largest generics market but a price-taker business: buyer consortia force prices down every year and profits come from a few products with limited competition. Zydus's prescriptions grew 6% a year over four years against 2% for the market, and it ranks #3. But the profit pool of FY23-FY26 came from gRevlimid and generic Myrbetriq. The industry is also moving into biosimilars (Zydus launched ranibizumab in Q1FY27) and 505(b)(2) specialty products, where competition is thinner.

**Consumer health and medtech.** India's packaged-wellness categories (sugar substitutes, glucose powder, health drinks, skin care) are growing with modern trade and e-commerce (38% of Zydus Wellness sales); European digital vitamins (Comfort Click) grew 25-31% like-for-like. Orthopaedic implants in Europe grow low-to-mid single digits with periodic French price cuts (3-4% in FY26).

bullets: **India chronic and specialty:** an ageing, diabetic population, government cancer schemes and first-wave biosimilars. Zydus is #1 in oncology and has two in-house NCEs on the market.

**The rupee:** ₹88.3/US$ on average in FY26, ₹95.81 on 30-Sep-2026. About 55% of revenue is earned abroad, so a weaker rupee lifts reported sales and margins (₹1,198 cr of forex gains in FY26 EBITDA).
**US specialty and biosimilars:** a changing FDA framework for biosimilars and Medicare Part B oncology access (Rolvedon) give mid-sized companies a way past plain generics.
**The end of limited-competition windfalls:** gRevlimid volume limits ended in Jan-2026; generic Myrbetriq competition grows; price erosion in the US base business is single-digit a year.
**Regulation:** USFDA inspections can block launches (Zydus's Jarod injectables site was cleared only after its Sep-2025 inspection); India's price controls and trade-generic growth limit pricing.
**US policy and litigation:** tariffs on pharmaceuticals were debated in 2025-26; Zydus is a defendant in the US generic price-fixing bellwether trials (2026-2028).

blocks.p: India formulations were ₹6,574 cr in FY26 (+11%) and grew 20% in Q1FY27, beating the market in cardiology, diabetes, gynaecology, pain, oncology and nephrology. Management guides mid-teens growth for FY27, 300-500bp above the market. International markets (emerging markets plus Europe) grew from ₹2,195 cr to ₹3,070 cr in FY26 (+40%) and +34% in Q1FY27 to US$100 mn+ a quarter: France and Spain recovered, the UK scaled "much faster than expected" and new countries took Zydus's first-generic and innovative launches. blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Zydus has a moat in India (brands, oncology leadership, a real innovation engine) and a good compliance record. sections.title: Revenue up 1.9x and EBITDA 2.5x since FY21; FY26 was the peak, Q1FY27 the reset

blocks.p: Zydus grew revenue from ₹14,404 cr in FY21 to ₹27,148 cr in FY26 (about 13% a year) and company-basis EBITDA from ₹3,391 cr to ₹8,475 cr. The margin went from 24% in FY21 (22% in FY22) to 31%. Three things did it: generic Revlimid (gRevlimid, a limited-competition US launch from Mar-2022), the semi-exclusive generic Myrbetriq (mirabegron), and India growing faster than its market. Two flattered FY26 further: a weaker rupee produced ₹1,198 cr of operating forex gains inside EBITDA, and acquisitions added ₹2,000 cr of revenue (Amplitude, Comfort Click). Reported EPS moved from ₹20.8 (FY21) to ₹50.1 (FY26); before one-offs it moved from ₹23.5 to ₹54.2.

blocks.p: Company-basis EBITDA margin went from 21.9% (FY22) to 27.5% (FY24), 30.4% (FY25) and 31.2% (FY26), then 24.1% in Q1FY27. Gross margin tells the same story: 72.7% in FY25 and 73.1% in FY26, 72.1% in Q1FY27 as gRevlimid left and the Mirabegron per-unit licence fee entered cost of goods. Two other things moved the line. Zydus books exchange gains inside other expenses: ₹1,198 cr in FY26, 4.4% of revenue, up to 8 points in a single quarter (Q4FY26). And acquisitions added costs faster than profit: other expenses excluding R&D rose 45-50% YoY in Q1FY27, about 80% of it from deals (CFO).

sections.title: From cash-rich to acquisitive: ₹7,000+ cr of deals and a ₹1,100 cr buyback in 15 months

blocks.p: Over FY21-26 Zydus generated ₹20,181 cr of operating cash flow, spent ₹8,361 cr on fixed assets and paid ₹2,670 cr of dividends. Until FY25 it was building cash: net cash was ~₹4,900 cr at Mar-25. Then it changed course. In FY26 it bought Amplitude Surgical (₹2,570 cr), Comfort Click through Zydus Wellness (₹2,877 cr) and the Agenus plants (₹1,080 cr), settled Mirabegron (₹1,060 cr incl. the prepaid licence), and in Q1FY27 bought Assertio (US$166 mn) and bought back ₹1,100 cr of shares. Net debt was ₹5,904 cr at Jun-26 (0.7x EBITDA). FY26 operating cash flow fell to ₹2,117 cr (25% of EBITDA) on the settlement and acquired working capital.

**We would move to HOLD above a target-to-price gap of −5%, i.e. a price below ~₹1,000,** and to BUY below ~₹830 on today's numbers, or sooner if Saroglitazar's launch and US$ sales beat our base.

**This is mostly a valuation call.** Our FY28E EPS is ~11% below the post-Q1 street, but the bigger gap is the multiple: the street pays 23-25x one-year-forward EPS; Zydus's own history supports ~19.5x after the sector re-rating. At the street's 23x on our Sep-28E EPS the stock would be worth ~₹1,120, roughly today's price: there is no upside even on the street's multiple.
**Biggest swing factors:** the multiple (each 1x is ~₹48 a share) and the US (each US$10 mn a quarter is ~₹33 a share at our multiple).

**Where we could be wrong:** our EV/EBITDA and DCF cross-checks (₹1,215 and ₹1,183) say the business is worth more if the acquisitions' amortisation and interest are temporary costs of growth. If Zydus proves that in FY28-29, the right multiple is the street's, not its history.

otherIncomeBuild._why: Treasury: FY26 interest income Rs422.5 cr was earned on ~Rs8,000 cr of average gross cash and investments, part of it an arbitrage of short-term borrowing against government securities (CFO, Aug-2025); the quarterly run-rate was Rs109-134 cr in FY26 and Rs106 cr in Q1FY27 (Rs424 cr annualised); it drifts down as acquisitions and the buyback use cash and short-term debt is repaid. JV: Rs57.8 cr (FY25), Rs97.1 cr (FY26), Rs37.8 cr (Q1FY27). Licence: Rs662.5 cr over 19 months from 10-Feb-2026 = Rs34.9 cr a month: Rs57.5 cr in FY26, Rs418.4 cr in FY27, Rs186.6 cr in FY28 (AR FY26 note 30).

taxBuild._note: Engine tax rate = (tax on PBT ex-JV + minorities) / PBT incl. JV. Rs crore.
taxBuild._why: Zydus owns 57.59% of Zydus Wellness (AR FY26 note 49; the promoter group's 69.63% includes other family entities). Zydus Wellness PAT: Rs346.9 cr (FY25), Rs197.2 cr (FY26, after Comfort Click acquisition interest and amortisation), Rs119 cr in Q1FY27 (its seasonal peak quarter). Minorities were Rs147.1 cr (FY25), Rs83.5 cr (FY26) and Rs50.4 cr (Q1FY27). We assume Zydus Wellness PAT recovers to Rs260 / 330 / 400 cr with Comfort Click growth and deleveraging.

dcf._betaWhy: Pharma is defensive (below-market sensitivity); modest leverage (net debt ~0.7x EBITDA at Jun-26). Beta 0.85 gives a cost of equity of 11.6%; the engine discounts at the cost of equity, which is close to a WACC with ~5% debt in the capital structure.
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; Zydus is half US generics (low single-digit growth in dollars, ~2% rupee depreciation) and half branded India/EM/consumer (high single digit). House range 5-6%: 5.5%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% (FY29E) to 7% over 15 years.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades from 24.5% to 25%: the branded mix rises (management aims for 28-30%), but US generic price erosion and new launches' costs recur; we do not assume the 31% of FY26, which included gRevlimid and Rs1,280 cr of forex gains.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex moves from ~4% of revenue (FY28-29E) to 4.5%: FY26 organic capex of Rs1,715 cr (6.3% of revenue) included new plants; maintenance plus growth capex for a branded-plus-generics portfolio is ~4.5%.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Saroglitazar is approved on time and launches well in PBC (heading to the upper end of the US$200-300 mn peak range), US generics hold US$330 mn+ a quarter as Mirabegron competition stays limited, India keeps growing ~15% and international markets ~20%; EBITDA margin climbs back above 25% by FY28-29E.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Saroglitazar is delayed or launches slowly against two entrenched PPAR agonists, gMirabegron and other key US products erode faster (US sales back to ~US$280 mn a quarter), the acquired businesses (Comfort Click, Amplitude, Zylidac) disappoint and an FDA problem hits a key site; EBITDA margin ~22%, the FY22-FY23 level.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Zydus: P/E on 12-month-forward or FY28E consolidated EPS (PL 25x FY28E, MOSL 23x 12-month forward, JM 24x Mar-28, Sharekhan 20x FY28E). Our multiple: Zydus's own one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 on EPS before exceptional items and the FY22 animal-health sale gain (trough years excluded), times the pharma sector factor (+5.45%, PLAYBOOK §7c), nearest half-turn. Applied to EPS per post-buyback share (99.75 cr shares); the engine carries it as an implied multiple of its own Sep-28E EPS (on the FY26 count of 100.62 cr shares), written by tools/authoring/ZYDUSLIFE.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Own trailing EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021 times the same sector factor, restated from trailing to Sep-28E EBITDA (ZYDUSLIFE.ctx.js). Adds the engine's net cash at Sep-28E; the engine does not deduct the Zydus Wellness minority, so the value is shown before and after that deduction in the report.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether Zydus's cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, cost of equity 11.6%, terminal growth 5.5%, plus the engine's net cash at Mar-27.
